explanation.text: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar Yaghi for the development of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), as confirmed by the Nobel Prize press release and the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announcement in Stockholm, Sweden.
The award recognizes the creation of porous molecular architectures (MOFs) with applications in gas storage, carbon capture, and catalysis, as detailed in the official announcement spans.
The announcement was made on 8 October 2025 by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, consistent with the standard venue for Nobel Chemistry Prizes in Stockholm, Sweden.

excerpts.text: [The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](http://www.kva.se/en/) has decided to award the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2025 to

**Susumu Kitagawa**, **Richard Robson** and **Omar Yaghi** are awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2025. They have developed a new form of molecular architecture. In their constructions, metal ions function as cornerstones that are linked by long organic (carbon-based) molecules. Together, the metal ions and molecules are organised to form crystals that contain large cavities. These porous materials are called metal–organic frameworks (MOF). By varying the building blocks used in the MOFs, chemists can design them to capture and store specific substances. MOFs can also drive chemical reactions or conduct electricity.
Following the laureates’ groundbreaking discoveries, chemists have built tens of thousands of different MOFs.
